blocks.goal: Extract a cohesive File state holder to reduce the number of fields and related accessors in FileEntry. Move the file attribute fields and their getters/setters/refresh logic into a new FileEntryAttributes class in the same package.

ops.details: Create a new class FileEntryAttributes in package org.apache.commons.io.monitor. The class will encapsulate the following fields: String name; boolean exists; boolean directory; SerializableFileTime lastModified; long length. It will provide the moved accessors and mutators: getName(), setName(String), isExists(), setExists(boolean), isDirectory(), setDirectory(boolean), getLastModified(), getLastModifiedFileTime(), setLastModified(FileTime), setLastModified(long), setLastModified(SerializableFileTime) (package-private or public as needed), getLength(), setLength(long). Move the refresh(File) implementation that reads the File to update these fields and returns a boolean indicating change (use Files.exists(file.toPath()), file.isDirectory(), FileUtils.lastModifiedFileTime(file) and file.length()). The class will import java.io.File, java.io.IOException, java.nio.file.Files, java.nio.file.attribute.FileTime and org.apache.commons.io.FileUtils and org.apache.commons.io.file.attribute.FileTimes and will use SerializableFileTime the same way as FileEntry. Put the new file in the same package (org.apache.commons.io.monitor). Ensure exception handling mirrors the original refresh implementation.

blocks.goal: Reduce FileEntry's API surface and complexity by delegating attribute storage and attribute-related behavior to the new FileEntryAttributes class. Update constructors and all callers inside FileEntry to use the new attributes holder.

ops.details: Add import for the newly created attributes holder: import org.apache.commons.io.monitor.FileEntryAttributes;

Remove the duplicated fields name, exists, directory, lastModified and length from FileEntry and add a single final field: private final FileEntryAttributes attributes;. Initialize attributes in each constructor: attributes = new FileEntryAttributes(); attributes.setName(file.getName()); (or call an appropriate constructor on FileEntryAttributes). Do not change parent, children, file fields.

Replace attribute access and methods in FileEntry to delegate to the attributes holder: - getName() -> return attributes.getName(); - isExists() -> return attributes.isExists(); - isDirectory() -> return attributes.isDirectory(); - getLastModified() -> return attributes.getLastModified(); - getLastModifiedFileTime() -> return attributes.getLastModifiedFileTime(); - getLength() -> return attributes.getLength(); - setName(String) -> attributes.setName(name); - setExists(boolean) -> attributes.setExists(exists); - setDirectory(boolean) -> attributes.setDirectory(directory); - setLastModified(FileTime) / setLastModified(long) -> delegate to attributes; - setLength(long) -> attributes.setLength(length); - refresh(File) -> delegate to attributes.refresh(file) and preserve behavior (this means refresh returns attributes.refresh(file)). Keep methods unrelated to attributes (getChildren, getFile, getLevel, getParent, newChildInstance, setChildren) unchanged except for any use of moved fields. Ensure any package-private usage of SerializableFileTime is contained in the new class. Update constructor(s) to set attributes name and initial values (e.g., attributes.setName(file.getName()); attributes.setExists(...); attributes.setDirectory(...); attributes.setLastModified(...); attributes.setLength(...)) if initial eager setup is required. Update any equality comparisons to use attributes' getters instead of now-removed fields.

Update related tests affected by this refactoring block so the configured build command passes. Adjust imports, package references, moved class references, constructors, and assertions only when required. Do not change production behavior through tests.
